text: Chance favors only the prepared mind.
where: Lecture at the University of Lille, December 7, 1854

text: A rising tide lifts all the boats.
where: Remarks at the dedication of Greers Ferry Dam, Heber Springs, Arkansas, October 3, 1963

text: Neither a borrower nor a lender be; for loan oft loses both itself and friend.
The rich ruleth over the poor, and the borrower is servant to the lender.
Beware of little expenses; a small leak will sink a great ship.
Rather go to bed supperless than rise in debt.
Creditors have better memories than debtors.
A fool and his money are soon parted.
where: Five Hundred Points of Good Husbandry (1573)

text: It is the part of a wise man to keep himself today for tomorrow, and not venture all his eggs in one basket.
Never spend your money before you have it.
where: Letter to Thomas Jefferson Smith, February 21, 1825

text: Penny wise and pound foolish.
The first thing is character... before money or anything else. Money cannot buy it.
where: Testimony to the Pujo Committee, U.S. House of Representatives, 1912

text: Price is what you pay. Value is what you get.
Be fearful when others are greedy, and be greedy only when others are fearful.
Cash is king.
Don't throw good money after bad.
Save for a rainy day.
Pay yourself first.
Measure twice, cut once.
Penny wise, pound foolish.
Never borrow short to lend long.
You can't manage what you don't measure.
If it sounds too good to be true, it probably is.
Get it in writing.
